title: Convexity in Lean: short proofs with every step visible
scope: Real functions, explicit Jensen inequalities, closure properties, and optimization certificates. No calculus, measure theory, or Langevin machinery is required.

setup.title: Files and names
setup.explanation: Each import loads checked declarations from another module. The namespace gives the project declarations a shared prefix. Comments describe the code and are not proof commands.

tokens.explanation: Load Definitions.lean and its imported declarations. Dots in a project module name correspond to folders.
Prefix declared names with ConvexityTutorial.; end ConvexityTutorial closes this naming scope.

setup.title: Read the types before reading the proof
setup.explanation: A type specifies what an input is. Propositions are also types: a proof of a proposition is an expression whose type is that proposition. Therefore hypotheses can be passed to lemmas just like numerical inputs.

tokens.explanation: The real numbers. The symbols and operations come from mathlib.

An explicit proof argument. The name hf is conventional; its declared type is what makes it a convexity proof.

∀ introduces arbitrary inputs. Between propositions, → introduces a premise that must be supplied as a proof.

setup.title: Definitions and anonymous functions
setup.explanation: A definition supplies an expression for a new name. An anonymous function supplies an input-to-output rule without introducing a separate named function.

tokens.explanation: Define the proposition IsConvex f by the quantified expression after :=.

tokens.explanation: The function sending x to s*x+c. The x after fun is bound only within this function expression.
A type annotation: one half is a real number. Lean can usually infer the types of other numerals from the expected real expressions.

setup.title: Theorem statements and goals
setup.explanation: A theorem names a proposition and provides its proof. A by block constructs that proof through tactics. Each displayed state lists the current context followed by ⊢ and the remaining proposition to prove.

tokens.explanation: Name the theorem, declare its data and proof inputs, state its conclusion, then begin constructing the proof.
The goal marker in the state display. It is not part of the theorem source.
Add a proved local fact with name h and proposition P. A nested by block proves P before returning to the surrounding goal.
The same construction, with the proposition inferred from the proof term.
More-indented tactics belong to a nested local proof. Dedenting returns to the surrounding proof.
Arguments separated by spaces are supplied from left to right, in the order of the lemma’s explicit binders. Some are real data and some are proofs.
False is the proposition with no proof; deriving it closes a contradiction. ¬ P means that a proof of P would imply False.

setup.title: Order steps and algebraic steps
setup.explanation: The proofs keep their mathematical reasons visible: convexity supplies inequalities; order lemmas combine them; rewriting uses equalities; arithmetic tactics check the remaining algebra. Every result is still checked by Lean’s kernel.

tokens.explanation: Rewrite with the named equalities in order. The equalities are used left to right in this tutorial.

Prove an exact numerical rational equality or inequality.
Prove the linear consequence or contradiction supplied by the current real equalities and inequalities.

lessons.title: Read a mathematical definition in Lean
lessons.why: The definition exposes every assumption of the chord inequality. Reading its binders correctly is enough to understand every convexity proof that follows.
lessons.statementMath: \operatorname{IsConvex}(f)\iff\forall x,y,a,b\in\mathbb R,\quad a\ge0,\ b\ge0,\ a+b=1\Longrightarrow f(ax+by)\le af(x)+bf(y)
